# Ollama desktop app: settings / network exposure / model dir — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Ollama desktop app: settings / network exposure / model dir. Run status: COMPLETED.

## How it works

- [statement] When Ollama runs as the macOS application, set environment variables with `launchctl setenv` (e.g. `launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST "0.0.0.0:11434"`) and restart the Ollama app. The menu-bar app is launched by launchd, not the shell, so exports in ~/.zshrc are not seen. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama desktop app: settings / network exposure / model dir · also: https://modelpiper.com/blog/ollama-environment-variables
- [statement] On Windows, change the model directory by setting OLLAMA_MODELS as a user-account environment variable (Settings or Control Panel, 'Edit environment variables for your account'), then quit the tray app and relaunch it from the Start menu or open a new terminal. Same mechanism applies to OLLAMA_HOST. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/windows · keywords: Ollama desktop app: settings / network exposure / model dir · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The server reads environment variables once at launch, so a changed OLLAMA_HOST or OLLAMA_MODELS only takes effect after Ollama is restarted. An unparseable port in OLLAMA_HOST logs a warning and silently reverts to the default instead of failing. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-22) — https://modelpiper.com/blog/ollama-environment-variables · keywords: Ollama desktop app: settings / network exposure / model dir · also: https://docs.ollama.com/windows

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Ollama binds 127.0.0.1 port 11434 by default; the bind address is changed with the OLLAMA_HOST environment variable (for example 0.0.0.0:11434 to listen on all interfaces). (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama desktop app: settings / network exposure / model dir · also: https://modelpiper.com/blog/ollama-environment-variables
- [statement] Default model directories: macOS ~/.ollama/models, Linux (service install) /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models, Windows C:\Users\%username%\.ollama\models. Setting OLLAMA_MODELS overrides it. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama desktop app: settings / network exposure / model dir · also: https://docs.ollama.com/macos
- [statement] OLLAMA_ORIGINS controls which browser origins may call the API and is separate from OLLAMA_HOST. Defaults allow 127.0.0.1 and 0.0.0.0 origins; extra origins such as chrome-extension://* must be added explicitly. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama desktop app: settings / network exposure / model dir · also: https://modelpiper.com/blog/ollama-environment-variables
- [statement] On macOS and Windows the Ollama app registers as a login item at install. It can be disabled (Windows Task Manager Startup apps; macOS Settings, Login Items, 'Allow in the Background'), and the setting is respected across upgrades unless the app is uninstalled. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] The Windows installer does not need Administrator, installs to the home directory by default, and accepts `OllamaSetup.exe /DIR="d:\some\location"` to relocate binaries. Models are stored separately via OLLAMA_MODELS, and uninstalling does not remove models stored at a custom OLLAMA_MODELS location. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/windows
- [statement] App and server logs: macOS ~/.ollama/logs/app.log and server.log; Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama\app.log and server.log. Models and config live in ~/.ollama (macOS) and %HOMEPATH%\.ollama (Windows). (medium confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/macos · keywords: Ollama desktop app: settings / network exposure / model dir · also: https://docs.ollama.com/windows
- [statement] Official docs document the desktop app's Settings only for context length (launch post, July 2025) and sign-in to Ollama cloud (Settings page on Mac and Windows). Neither the launch post nor the macOS and Windows docs pages mention an app setting for network exposure or model location. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://ollama.com/blog/new-app · keywords: Ollama desktop app: settings / network exposure / model dir · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] Ollama's HTTP API has no authentication by default; binding OLLAMA_HOST to 0.0.0.0 lets anyone who can reach the port use it. Guard it with a firewall or a reverse proxy such as Nginx (the FAQ shows a proxy config). (medium confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama desktop app: settings / network exposure / model dir · also: https://modelpiper.com/blog/ollama-environment-variables
- [statement] Third-party guides say newer macOS and Windows desktop apps have a Settings toggle 'Expose Ollama to the network'. This came only from search-result snippets; the guide page returned HTTP 403 and no official page confirms it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.digitalcitizen.life/how-to-expose-ollama-to-the-network-on-windows/
